note: Seed hypotheses from the Shorts hook research and the Kylo digest. No results: every `result` is null and every decision OPEN. Copy to <world>/experiments.json with `experiments.py init`.

experiments.claim: A voice line starting by 0.5 s (no pre-roll silence) keeps more viewers than one starting after 1.5 s.
experiments.test_plan: Two Shorts of the same quality, voice at 0.3 s vs 1.5 s; same cast and length class.

experiments.claim: Opening on the funniest standalone sentence beats opening on narration.
experiments.test_plan: Alternate the two openings across episodes; compare viewed-vs-swiped.

experiments.claim: A reverse cold open (aftermath first) beats a linear open for story sketches.
A Short with no intro screen and at most a 0.5 s sting at the end retains better than one with a 1-3 s title card.
experiments.test_plan: A/B on two uploads: no intro vs 2 s card; compare viewed-vs-swiped.

experiments.claim: A brand sound of 0.3-0.5 s on the last frame costs nothing and builds recognition.
experiments.test_plan: Episodes with and without the sting; compare avg view percentage.

experiments.claim: Burned-in karaoke subtitles, 1-3 words, speaker colour, accent on the punch word, beat plain white subtitles.
experiments.test_plan: Alternate styles across episodes of one format.

experiments.claim: Subtitles at 55-70% of frame height avoid the UI overlay and read better than the default caption zone.
experiments.test_plan: Upload a test grid first (no official pixel spec), then compare retention between zones.

experiments.claim: A cover with the hero large on the left, up to 8 words, key word accented, converts better than a frame grab.
experiments.test_plan: Alternate cover styles; compare impressions click-through where the cover shows (feed/search).

experiments.claim: A 55 s cut of a dialogue sketch beats the full 3 min as a Short on viewed-vs-swiped and average view percentage.
experiments.test_plan: Publish the 55 s cut and the full 3 min of comparable sketches; compare.

experiments.claim: A seamless loop (last line links to the first frame) raises average view percentage above 100.
experiments.test_plan: Episodes with and without a loop bridge in the button; compare avg view percentage.

experiments.claim: A deliberate re-hook at 8-15 s (new info, voice or visual) lifts retention at 10 s.
experiments.test_plan: Episodes with and without a marked re-hook rung.

experiments.claim: A spoken subscribe line lowers late retention; an on-screen comment question does not.
experiments.test_plan: Spoken CTA vs on-screen question vs none.

experiments.claim: Numbering episodes in the title and the corner mark builds a series without intro time.
experiments.test_plan: Numbered vs unnumbered titles on comparable episodes.

experiments.claim: Blog thresholds (70% viewed good, 75-80% strong) hold for our channel.
experiments.test_plan: Collect our own first 10 episodes; set our own baseline; do not judge a hook before it exists.

experiments.claim: The Russian-language Shorts feed behaves like the global benchmarks.
experiments.test_plan: Compare our baseline against the 3P numbers once there is one.

experiments.claim: A cast-and-rig series passes the repetitive-content rule when each episode changes mechanism and outcome.
experiments.test_plan: Keep the distinct check green across a run of episodes; watch Studio monetisation notices; any notice is the result.
